message.content:
To evaluate the definite integral  

\[
\int_{1}^{3} x^{2}\,dx ,
\]

we first find an antiderivative of \(f(x)=x^{2}\).  
A convenient antiderivative is

\[
F(x)=\frac{x^{3}}{3},
\]

since \(\displaystyle F'(x)=x^{2}\).

Now apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus:

\[
\int_{1}^{3} x^{2}\,dx = F(3)-F(1)
= \frac{3^{3}}{3}-\frac{1^{3}}{3}
= \frac{27}{3}-\frac{1}{3}
= 9-\frac{1}{3}
= \frac{27-1}{3}
= \frac{26}{3}.
\]

So the value of the definite integral is  

\[
\boxed{\dfrac{26}{3}}\approx 8.67 .
\]
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Find the definite integral of f(x)=x^2 from x=1 to x=3." They want the definite integral ∫_1^3 x^2 dx. That equals [x^3/3]_1^3 = (27/3) - (1/3) = 9 - 1/3 = 26/3 ≈ 8.6667.
